encounters.cc: Chronic pain in right groin and buttock exacerbated by walking and climbing stairs

lines: Chronic pain in right groin and buttock exacerbated by walking and climbing stairs
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of chronic pain in her right groin and buttock.
She reports that the pain is exacerbated by walking and climbing stairs and is relieved by rest.
She denies any recent trauma or injury.
She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
- Right total knee arthroplasty (post-operative week 1 at presentation)
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 12 years ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
On physical examination, you note that her right hip has a decreased range of motion, particularly with internal rotation.
There is no erythema, warmth, or swelling.
An X-ray of the hip is performed, which shows:
- Osteophyte formation at the acetabular rim

encounters.cc: Difficulty reading and recognizing faces over the past six months with central vision changes

lines: Difficulty reading and recognizing faces over the past six months with central vision changes
The patient returns for follow-up of her known macular degeneration three months after orthopedic evaluation for hip osteoarthritis.
She reports that her vision problems are affecting both eyes and are more pronounced in the center of her visual field.
She denies any pain or redness in her eyes.
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril, and hypercholesterolemia, managed with atorvastatin.
- Right total knee arthroplasty (post-operative week 1 at presentation)
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
She has a 30-pack-year smoking history but quit 10 years ago.
On physical examination, her visual acuity is 20/40 in both eyes.
Amsler grid testing reveals metamorphopsia centrally in both eyes.
Fundoscopic examination shows bilateral drusen and pigmentary changes in the macula.
There are no signs of hemorrhage or exudate.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and confusion on postoperative day 4 following right total knee replacement

lines: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and confusion on postoperative day 4 following right total knee replacement

This 65-year-old female with chronic atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation and severe osteoarthritis, previously evaluated for hip arthritis and macular degeneration, is brought to the emergency department after developing sudden-onset shortness of breath and confusion on postoperative day 4 following a right total knee replacement.
She has been recovering with limited ambulation.
Her medical history includes hypertension and osteoarthritis.
- Right total knee arthroplasty (post-operative week 1 at presentation)
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 12 years ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
Her temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure is 90/58 mm Hg, pulse is 122/min, and respiratory rate is 30/min.
Her lungs are clear to auscultation, and heart sounds are normal.
There is mild swelling and tenderness of the right calf.
Arterial blood gas on room air shows: pH 7.47, PaCO₂ 27 mm Hg, PaO₂ 60 mm Hg.

encounters.cc: Severe pain, redness, and swelling in right knee for 2 days without trauma

lines: Severe pain, redness, and swelling in right knee for 2 days without trauma
The patient with calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease and prior right knee replacement presents with acute symptoms.
She reports that the pain began suddenly and has progressively worsened.
She denies any recent trauma but mentions she was hospitalized 3 weeks ago for a urinary tract infection and treated with antibiotics.
- Right total knee arthroplasty (post-operative week 1 at presentation)
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 12 years ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
On physical examination, her right knee is warm, erythematous, and swollen with decreased range of motion due to pain.
Aspiration of the knee joint yields synovial fluid that is yellow and cloudy.
- Negative for organisms on Gram stain
Radiographs of the right knee show chondrocalcinosis.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of sharp, right-sided chest pain worsening with inspiration and shortness of breath

lines: Sudden onset of sharp, right-sided chest pain worsening with inspiration and shortness of breath
The patient with recurrent VTE and AFib presents with acute chest pain.
She returned from a transatlantic flight 3 days prior, which lasted 8 hours, and has been mostly bedridden since due to a mild flu.
Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
- Right total knee arthroplasty (post-operative week 1 at presentation)
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 12 years ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
Tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 24 breaths/min, and tachycardic with a heart rate of 110 beats/min.
Oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
A lower extremity examination reveals mild right calf swelling with tenderness to palpation.
No skin changes or palpable cords are noted.
Lung auscultation is clear, and there is no jugular venous distension.
An electrocardiogram shows sinus tachycardia with no ST changes.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue, unintentional 8-kg weight loss over 3 months, and dry cough

lines: Progressive fatigue, unintentional 8-kg weight loss over 3 months, and dry cough

The patient, with chronic atrial fibrillation on warfarin and prior pulmonary emboli in 2020 and 2021, reports increasing shortness of breath with activity, occasional dry cough, and vague right-sided chest discomfort.
She denies fever, night sweats, or hemoptysis.
Her medical history is notable for hypertension and osteoarthritis.
- Right total knee arthroplasty (post-operative week 1 at presentation)
Her medications include lisinopril and acetaminophen.
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
She quit smoking 12 years ago after a 30-pack-year history.
She lives alone and retired from her job as a librarian last year.
She has no known occupational exposures.
Vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, she appears thin but alert.
There is digital clubbing of the fingers and decreased breath sounds at the right lung base.
No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is noted.
Laboratory studies are significant for mild anemia (Hb 10.8 g/dL) and slightly elevated alkaline phosphatase.
A chest x-ray reveals a solitary 3.5-cm peripheral opacity in the right lower lobe with associated pleural retraction.
CT scan confirms the mass and shows no hilar lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion.
CT-guided biopsy is performed, and histology reveals malignant gland-forming cells with mucin production.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of shortness of breath and sharp right-sided pleuritic chest pain

lines: Sudden onset of shortness of breath and sharp right-sided pleuritic chest pain
The patient with recurrent venous thromboembolism and Stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer presents with acute symptoms.
She reports that she was recovering well until this morning when she suddenly felt a sharp pain on the right side of her chest, which worsens with deep breaths.
She denies any cough or fever.
- Stage IIIB Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
Recent total hip replacement surgery 2 weeks ago
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (dose adjusted per INR)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 12 years ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
Tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, her heart rate is 110 beats per minute, blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, and oxygen saturation is 89% on room air
Her jugular venous pressure is elevated, and lung auscultation reveals decreased breath sounds at the right lung base without wheezes or crackles.
Lower extremity examination shows mild right calf swelling with tenderness to palpation.
D-dimer level is elevated. Laboratory Values: - D-dimer: 0.8 mg/L (normal <0.5 mg/L)
Electrocardiogram (ECG) shows sinus tachycardia with no ST-segment or T-wave changes

encounters.cc: Acute onset of shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain beginning 2 hours ago

lines: Acute onset of shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain beginning 2 hours ago

This 68-year-old woman with recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain that started 2 hours ago.
- Stage IIIB Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
She has a past medical history of hypertension and chronic atrial fibrillation.
She recently underwent a total hip replacement 4 days ago.
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Paternal uncle: Myocardial infarction at age 55
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 12 years ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 glasses of wine weekly.
Respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, and oxygen saturation is 89% on room air
On examination, she is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, and oxygen saturation is 89% on room air.
Her jugular venous pressure is not elevated.
Lung auscultation reveals decreased breath sounds at the left lung base without wheezes or crackles.
The left lower extremity is swollen and tender to palpation.
A D-dimer test is markedly elevated.
An arterial blood gas shows hypoxemia with a PaO2 of 60 mmHg.
A CT pulmonary angiogram is performed and reveals a large embolus in the left pulmonary artery.
